reason: litellm 1.93.2 ships an optional Rust OCR bridge (litellm/rust_bridge/_native.cpython-312-*-linux-gnu.so) whose binary embeds the distrusted 'emSign ECC Root CA - G3' trust anchor (label grep: 1 match; the PEM body probe: 0). The bridge is never loaded by an agentfactory gateway, so the anchor is never placed in a trust store that the gateway uses.
evidence: The native module is imported only by litellm.rust_bridge.get_native_bridge (rust_bridge/loader.py), reached only through load_rust_ocr/load_rust_aocr, which litellm/ocr/main.py:399 calls only when rust_ocr_bridge.rust_ocr_enabled() is true. That flag is set only by the LITELLM_USE_RUST_OCR environment variable (rust_bridge/ocr.py:48-57) or a litellm.use_litellm_rust(True) call (rust_bridge/ocr.py:62). quickstart.sh's gateway launch lines export neither, and no agentfactory code calls use_litellm_rust (grep over quickstart.sh and internal/: 0). The agentfactory gateway has no user or key store, so no internal_user can exist; the only principal is the master key, which is already proxy_admin. Kept on 1.93.2 by operator decision D21 (2026-10-26). This does not claim the gateway is unexposed: it listens on the wildcard address.

reason: Environment-variable and file read through the Azure Entra ID credential parameters (tenant_id, client_id, client_secret, azure_username, azure_password, azure_scope), which the 1.93.2 request-body blocklist does not cover. It needs an authenticated low-privilege gateway principal: the advisory's impact is such a user reading the proxy's secrets, LITELLM_MASTER_KEY among them. The agentfactory gateway has no user or key store, so no such principal can exist; the only principal is the master key, which is already proxy_admin, and its holders (the agents) already read their key from the same secrets directory as the upstream credentials. The vendor scopes the advisory to deployments with an azure/ or azure_ai/ model, and no gateway config af writes has one, but this entry does not rely on that: a request-supplied custom_llm_provider can likely select the Azure provider for a listed model. Kept on 1.93.2 by operator decision D21 (2026-10-26). This does not claim the gateway is unexposed: it listens on the wildcard address.
evidence: Issue stempeck/agentfactory-pro#763. GitHub repository advisory BerriAI/litellm GHSA-2rwg-2wh4-7c4f, fetched 2026-11-13: severity high, CVSS 7.7, state published, no CVE assigned, patched_versions 1.106.9/1.108.6/1.109.1/1.110.0-rc.2. The first release the audit clears is 1.110.0-rc.2, with no stable 1.110.0 as of 2026-11-13. Both gateway configs quickstart.sh writes (the api-key heredoc, quickstart.sh:2399-2442, and subscription_yaml_body, :2457-2511) and the af install --init seed .agentfactory/litellm.yaml set general_settings.master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY and no database_url, and neither launch line (:2637, :2646) exports DATABASE_URL. In litellm 1.93.2, /key/generate and /user/new refuse with db_not_connected_error when there is no database (proxy/management_endpoints/key_management_endpoints.py:1550-1554, internal_user_endpoints.py:413-414), so no non-admin principal can be created. The agent profiles authenticate with the master key file .agentfactory/secrets/litellm.key (quickstart.sh:2534, :2548), in the chmod 700 .agentfactory/secrets directory (:2229, :2304) that also holds the upstream credentials. The blocklist gap is real: _BANNED_REQUEST_BODY_PARAMS (proxy/auth/auth_utils.py:253-302, including its derived observability and custom-pricing sets) names none of the six Entra parameters, which the Azure provider reads (llms/azure/common_utils.py:283-291), and does not ban custom_llm_provider, which litellm.completion takes from the request (main.py:4980). Source read from the sha256-verified PyPI wheel litellm-1.93.2-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl. TestGatewayConfigHasNoUserDatabase pins the no-database fact.

reason: HTML injection into organization-invitation emails.
